newsitem.title: SYRIA: Eight Arab countries agree to form common market.
newsitem.headline: Eight Arab countries agree to form common market.

text.p: The foreign ministers of Syria, Egypt and six Gulf Arab states ended talks in the Syrian resort of Latakia on Thursday by agreeing to set up a common market among the eight countries.

A communique issued by ministers of the so-called Damascus Declaration grouping said the ministers had assigned a committee to meet before September to prepare measures for the establishment of the market.

The ministers also expressed deep concern over Turkish-Israeli military and security cooperation, which "constitutes a threat to the security of Arab countries and to stability in the Middle East", the communique said.

The ministers "called on Turkey, a member of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference, to reconsider its cooperation pact with Israel and to return to the ties of good neighbourliness and cooperation with Arab countries, to preserve the mutual interests and the historical links between the two sides".
The ministers also "jointly rejected attempts by the Israeli government to avoid its commitment to withdraw fully from the Golan (Heights) to the June 4, 1967 (pre-war) boundaries".

In an indirect reference to Qatar's plans to hold a Middle East and North Africa economic summit in September, the communique stressed the need for Arab countries to abide by resolutions adopted by the Arab League in March regarding normalisation with Israel and regional cooperation.
